questions.q: Who is called the father of modern chemistry?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Antoine Lavoisier is called the father of modern chemistry.

questions.q: Who was the first one to propose a model for the structure of an atom ?
questions.explanation: The first person to propose a model for the structure of the atom was J. J. Thomson. In 1898, he proposed the plum pudding model. This model has been given different names, for example—plum pudding model, raisin pudding model, or watermelon model. In this model, the positive charge of the atom is considered like a pudding or a watermelon, in which electrons are present like plums or seeds. An important feature of this model is that the mass of the atom is assumed to be uniformly distributed throughout the atom. Although this model explained the electrical neutrality of the atom, it was not found consistent with the results of later experiments.

questions.q: Dalton’s atomic theory successfully explained (i) Law of conservation of mass. (ii) Law of constant composition. (iii) Law of radioactivity. (iv) Law of multiple proportions.
questions.explanation: 1. John Dalton presented the atomic theory in 1803, in which he gave important facts about the nature of matter. According to Dalton’s atomic theory, matter is made up of indivisible particles called atoms. 2. All atoms of an element are identical in size, mass, and chemical properties. 3. Atoms of different elements are different from each other. 4. In chemical reactions, atoms only get rearranged. 5. In compounds, atoms of different elements combine in simple whole-number ratios. 6. Dalton’s atomic theory successfully explained the law of conservation of mass, the law of constant composition (definite proportions), and the law of multiple proportions. Law of conservation of mass – According to the law of conservation of mass, matter can neither be created nor destroyed. Law of definite proportions – This law was given by the French chemist Joseph Proust. According to him, in a compound, the ratio of masses of the elements is always constant. Law of multiple proportions – The law of multiple proportions was given by Dalton in 1803. According to this law, if two elements combine to form more than one compound, then the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other element are in the ratio of small whole numbers. Therefore, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q: Particles which can be added to the nucleus of an atom without changing its chemical properties are

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: If neutrons are added to the nucleus of an atom, the chemical properties remain unchanged. The nucleus is made up of nuclear particles—protons and neutrons. These particles are called nucleons.

questions.q: The positively charged part at the centre of an atom is called as :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The positively charged part at the centre of an atom is called the nucleus. The nucleus is the central core of the atom. In the nucleus, protons and neutrons are present and are called nucleons. A proton is a positively charged particle, and a neutron is neutral; therefore, the nucleus is positively charged. The mass of protons and neutrons (approximately the same) is 1.67 × 10-27 kg, and their discoveries are attributed to E. Goldstein and James Chadwick, respectively.

questions.q: Which subatomic particle has negligible mass?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: An electron is a negatively charged subatomic particle that moves around the atomic nucleus. The charge on an electron is −1.602×10−19 C. The mass of an electron is about 9×10−31 kg.

questions.q: Which of the following is an incorrect option?

options.A: The atom is electrically neutral due to the presence of protons and electrons inside the nucleus.
options.B: Electrons are negatively charged and have negligible mass.
options.C: Atomic number is the number of protons in an atom of an element.

questions.explanation: Among the given statements, option (a) is not correct, because an atom is electrically neutral due to an equal number of protons (positively charged particles) and electrons (negatively charged particles). However, the nucleus contains only protons and neutrons, while electrons are present in orbits outside the nucleus. The statements in options (b), (c), and (d) are correct.

questions.q: Which fundamental particles are present in the nucleus of an atom?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The atomic nucleus is made up of protons and neutrons. The mass of the nucleus is due to protons and neutrons, and the positive charge of the nucleus is only due to protons. Protons and neutrons together are called nucleons, because they are the constituents of the atomic nucleus.

questions.q: The components of atomic nucleus are :
questions.explanation: The atomic nucleus is made up of protons and neutrons. The mass of the nucleus is due to protons and neutrons, and the positive charge of the nucleus is only due to protons. Protons and neutrons together are called nucleons, because they are the constituents of the atomic nucleus.

options.E: Copper

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.q: Isotopes of an element differ in -

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Elements having the same atomic number are called isotopes; that is, those whose atomic number (number of protons) is the same, but whose mass number or atomic weight is different, are called isotopes. Elements having the same atomic weight are called isobars. In isotopes, the number of protons is the same, but the number of neutrons is different.

questions.explanation: The electronic configuration 2, 8, 8, 2 is for an alkaline earth metal (calcium). The electronic configuration 2, 8 is for an inert gas (neon). The electronic configuration 2, 8, 7 is for chlorine (halogen). The electronic configuration 2, 8, 8 is for an inert gas (argon).

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The smallest particles of an element, which form molecules and take part in chemical reactions without being decomposed, are called atoms. Modern atomic symbols are based on the method proposed by Berzelius.

questions.q: Which of the following elements has the largest atomic radius?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Among the given elements, lithium has the largest atomic radius. The atomic radius of lithium is about 152 pm, the atomic radius of beryllium is 111 pm, and the atomic radius of boron is 88 pm. Here, pm means picometre.

questions.q: An example of physical change –
questions.explanation: A physical process is a process in which, on removing the cause, the substance involved returns to its original state. A physical process is temporary and reversible. Dissolving sugar in water is a physical change because sugar can be obtained again by evaporation.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a physical change?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Burning coal is an example of a chemical change, whereas melting of ice and dissolving salt in water are examples of physical changes. A chemical change occurs as a result of a chemical reaction, while a physical change occurs when the form changes but the chemical composition does not change.

questions.q: According to chemistry, which of the following is an example of a physical change?

options.D: Formation of a green layer on copper utensils
options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Boiling of water is a physical change because when heat is removed, the water vapor returns to its original state (water). Other examples—melting of ice, melting of wax, etc.

questions.q: What is the law in which under the same conditions of temperature and pressure, equal volumes of all gases contain equal number of molecules?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: According to Avogadro’s law, at the same temperature and pressure, equal volumes of all ideal gases contain the same number of particles or molecules. The number of molecules in one gram-mole of a gas is called the Avogadro number.

questions.explanation: When a gas changes into a liquid, this process is called condensation, that is condensation is the process in which vapour (gas) cools down and changes into the liquid state. Examples—clouds, fog, rain, etc.

questions.q: The amount of solute present per unit volume or per unit mass of the solution/solvent is known as _____ in Chemistry.
questions.explanation: The amount of solute present per unit volume or per unit mass is called the concentration of the solution in chemistry. A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more components. A homogeneous mixture means that the composition and properties are uniform throughout. Generally, the component present in larger quantity is called the solvent. The solvent determines the physical state in which the solution exists. Besides the solvent, one or more components present in the solution are called solutes.

questions.explanation: To obtain an ideal liquid (ideal solution) by mixing liquids A and B, the enthalpy of mixing must be zero. In an ideal solution, there is no interaction between molecules. Zero enthalpy means that during mixing, heat is neither absorbed nor released.

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The process of separating different liquid components of a mixture by adsorption on a suitable substance is called chromatography. This method is based on the fact that different components of a mixture have different adsorption capacities; therefore, they get adsorbed at different distances on an adsorbent substance and are thus separated.

Some solids, when heated, do not change into the liquid state; instead, they directly change into vapour, and on cooling, the vapour directly changes back into solid. options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

A bonding between constituent atoms or molecules takes place during crystallization. 3. It is an example of chemical change. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The process of obtaining crystals of pure substances from their solutions is called crystallization. During crystallization, van der Waals forces/interactions are established among the particles. No new chemical substance is formed in the process of crystallization. questions.q: Milk is an example of :

The solute-like component (dispersed particles) present in colloidal form is called the dispersed phase, and the component in which the dispersed phase remains suspended is called the dispersion medium. Colloidal solutions are classified on the basis of the physical state of the dispersion medium (solid, liquid, or gas) and the dispersed phase. questions.q: What physical process is the release of molecular oxygen from leaves?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

Diffusion is the process in which two or more substances mix spontaneously to form a homogeneous mixture. options.C: No net change in energy is involved

questions.explanation: Among the options given above, being irreversible, formation of new substances, and absorption of energy are characteristics of a chemical change, whereas “no net change in energy” is involved is not a characteristic of a chemical change.

questions.q: The process in which atmospheric carbon dioxide is converted into carbohydrates during photosynthesis is -

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: In the process of reduction, atmospheric carbon dioxide is converted into carbohydrates during photosynthesis. During photosynthesis, two substrates (CO2 and H2O) react in the presence of light to form two products (carbohydrates and oxygen).

questions.q: Which of the following pairs will give displacement reactions ?
questions.explanation: In a displacement reaction, a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from the solution of its salt. Copper (Cu) is more reactive than silver (Ag). Therefore, when copper metal is placed in a silver nitrate (AgNO3) solution, copper displaces silver and copper nitrate, [Cu(NO3)2], is formed. Cu + 2AgNO3 → Cu(NO3)2 + 2Ag Hence, the reaction between AgNO3 solution and copper metal is an example of a displacement reaction. Copper (Cu) is less reactive than sodium; therefore, it cannot displace sodium from sodium chloride (NaCl) solution. Copper (Cu) and silver (Ag) are both less reactive than iron (Fe); therefore, they cannot displace iron from iron sulphate (FeSO4) solution. Aluminium (Al) is less reactive than magnesium (Mg); therefore, it cannot displace magnesium from magnesium chloride (MgCl2) solution.

questions.q: The process in which oxidation number decreases is known as :

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: A reaction in which the oxidation number increases is called oxidation, and the one in which the oxidation number decreases is called reduction.

questions.q: In one of the following options, materials are arranged in increasing order of the force of attraction between their particles. Choose the correct option :
questions.explanation: The force acting between the molecules of a substance is called intermolecular force. It is maximum in solids and minimum in gases. In liquids, this force is greater than in gases but less than in solids. Therefore, among the given options, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q: In which of the following medicine production, ethyl alcohol can be used?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Ethyl alcohol or ethanol is used in the production of pharmaceuticals, polymers, leather, polish, plasticizers, cosmetics, etc. It is also used in the production of antiseptic, antipyretic, and anti allergic medicines.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a characteristic of a solid?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Solids do not have the ability to flow easily. A solid has a definite shape and volume. Solids are mainly of two types— crystalline solids and amorphous solids.

questions.q: Which of the following are exothermic processes ? (i) Evaporation of water. (ii) Dilution of an acid (H2SO4). (iii) Reaction of water with quick lime. (iv) Sublimation of camphor (crystals).
questions.explanation: Dilution of sulfuric acid (H2SO4) and the reaction of water with quicklime are examples of exothermic reactions. A chemical reaction in which heat is released along with the products is defined as an exothermic reaction.

questions.q: Which of the following represents the suitable condition for the liquefaction of gases ?
questions.explanation: For liquefaction of gases, the suitable condition is low temperature and high pressure. This is because, at high pressure and low temperature, gas molecules come closer to each other and their kinetic energy decreases; as a result, gases change into the liquid state.

questions.q: Which of the following are the constituents of a sodaacid fire extinguisher ?

options.D: Conc. sulphuric acid and sodium carbonate solution

questions.q: Full form of PHBV biodegradable polymer:

options.D: Poly hydroxy butyric acid veratric acid

questions.q: Blue vitriol is chemically :

questions.q: Which among the following is known as quicklime?

questions.q: Limewater is turned milky by:

questions.explanation: The first artificially prepared element is Technetium (Tc), whose atomic number is 43. Its molar mass is 98.91 g mol–¹. It was isolated in 1937 by Carlo Perrier and Emilio Segrè.

questions.q: Which of the following is the main ingredient of cement?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The main ingredient used in the manufacture of cement is limestone.

questions.q: In a car battery, electrolyte substance used is-
questions.explanation: A secondary cell is used in cars. These batteries are also called lead accumulators or storage batteries. Batteries used in cars, trucks, and inverters are examples of secondary batteries.

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: While galvanizing brass utensils, the smoke emanating from ammonium chloride powder used for cleaning the hot utensil is ammonia and hydrochloric acid.

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Hardness of water is due to the presence of soluble bicarbonates, chlorides and sulphates of calcium and magnesium. Chlorides and sulphates cause permanent hardness, which cannot be removed by boiling. questions.q: The trade name of alkaline (basic) lead carbonate is -

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: The commercial name of alkaline (basic) lead carbonate is Safeda (White lead). Its chemical formula is 2PbCO3·Pb(OH)2.

questions.q: Which of the following will have the maximum weight?
questions.explanation: Molecular weight of sucrose (C12H22O11) = 12 × atomic weight of C + 22 × atomic weight + 11 × atomic weight of O = (12×12) + (22×1) + (11×16) = 342 g/mol Weight of 0.2 mole of sucrose = 342 × 0.2 = 68.4 g Weight of CO2 = (12×1) + (16×2) = 44 g/mol Weight of 2 moles of CO2 = 44 × 2 = 88 g Weight of 2 moles of CaCO3 = 2 × [(1× atomic weight of Ca) + (1× atomic weight of C) + (3× atomic weight of O)] = 2 × (40 + 12 + 3×16) = 200 g Therefore, among the given options, the weight of 2 moles of CaCO3 is the maximum.

questions.q: Which of the following oxides is soluble in water?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Calcium oxide reacts with water to form calcium hydroxide [Ca(OH)2]; hence it is treated as soluble in water, whereas FeO and ZnO are not soluble in water. CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2 Therefore, the correct answer is option (c).

questions.q: Which of the following is not an electrophile?
questions.explanation: Na+ is not a true electrophile because it already has a stable outer-shell configuration. Electrophiles may be positively charged or may have vacant orbitals. H+ and BF3 – are examples of electrophiles.

questions.q: Which metal compound is used for the treatment of carcinoma?
questions.explanation: Carcinoma is a cancer that arises from the lining (epithelial tissue) of the skin or internal organs. Platinum-based compounds (mainly cisplatin, carboplatin, oxaliplatin) are widely used chemotherapy drugs for the treatment of carcinoma and many other solid tumours.

questions.q: The purest form of iron is

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The purest form of iron is wrought iron. Iron is the first element of the eighth group in the periodic table. Compared to pig iron, it is an alloy of iron with very low carbon content. Pig iron is also another form of iron, but it contains silicon, manganese, and traces of other elements; its carbon content is about 2–4%.

questions.q: Which of the following has highest melting point?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The melting point of a solid substance is the temperature at which it changes from the solid state to the liquid state. At the melting point, the solid and liquid phases remain in equilibrium. The melting point of boron is 2350 K, aluminium is 933.473 K, silicon is 1687 K, and iron is 1811 K. Hence, boron has the highest melting point.

questions.q: The chemical formula of sapphire (Ruby) is :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Sapphire is a gemstone mineral. Its chemical formula is Al2O3. Sapphire is found in nature and can also be made artificially. Note that sapphire and ruby are different.

questions.q: Which of the following corundum and cryolite are important ores ?
questions.explanation: Ore Chemical Formula Bauxite Al2O3·2H2O Cryolite Na3AlF6 Corundum Al2O3 Diaspore AlO (OH) Both corundum and cryolite are ores of aluminium metal. Bauxite and diaspore are other major ores of aluminium. s of

questions.q: Gases used in welding are :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Gas welding is a process in which metals are melted and joined or repaired through heat produced by the reaction of acetylene and oxygen. Oxy-acetylene welding is the most commonly used method.

questions.q: Why oil is not stored in galvanized iron pot?
questions.explanation: Galvanized iron is iron coated with a layer of zinc (Zn) to protect it from rusting. The zinc layer reacts with free fatty acids and moisture present in oil and forms toxic zinc compounds. Zinc salts and metal ions increase the rate of oxidation (rancidity) of oil, thereby reducing its quality. Due to these reactions, the protective zinc layer gradually gets corroded, and the iron underneath comes in contact with moisture and oxygen; as a result, corrosion and rust are clearly observed. Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.q: Galvanized iron pipes have a coating of :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The method of protecting iron and steel from rust by coating them with a thin layer of zinc is called galvanization.

questions.q: The element(s) that are excreted through human sweat is/are-

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Sweat mainly consists of water; however, it also contains minerals, acids, and urea. Sweat contains elements such as sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, zinc, iron, etc. Hence, option (e) is the required answer.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a non-ferrous metallic mineral?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A non-ferrous metallic mineral is a mineral that does not contain iron; for example—cobalt, tin, copper, zinc, etc. All minerals that contain iron are called ferrous metallic minerals; for example—manganese, nickel, chromium, etc.

questions.q: What is the glass used in tube lights and test tubes made of?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The glass used in tube lights and test tubes is an amorphous, transparent mixture of alkali metal silicates. It is prepared from silica, cerium oxide, sodium oxide, and other oxides.

questions.q: Which of the following metals has the highest electrical conductivity?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The order of electrical conductivity (from highest to lowest) among major metals is— Silver > Copper > Gold > Aluminium > Beryllium > Calcium.

questions.q: The heaviest metal among the following is :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Here, “heaviest” means “density”. Among the given options, platinum (Pt) has the highest density, about 21.45 g/cm³. Silver (Ag) has a density of about 10.5 g/cm³, mercury (Hg) about 13.54 g/cm³, and gold about 19.32 g/cm³.

questions.q: To protect broken bones, Plaster of Paris is used. It is :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Gypsum, whose chemical formula is CaSO4·2H2O, on heating loses water molecules and forms calcium sulfate hemihydrate (CaSO4 . 1 2 H2O). This is called “Plaster of Paris”. It is also used as bandages in surgery.

questions.q: The formula of Plaster of Paris is-
questions.explanation: The chemical formula of Plaster of Paris is CaSO4 . 1 2 H2O (calcium sulfate hemihydrate). It is formed by heating gypsum (calcium sulfate dihydrate). However, as per the options, it can also be written equivalently as (CaSO4)2·H2O.

questions.q: Minerals are-
questions.explanation: According to geologists, a “mineral” is a naturally occurring inorganic solid, having a crystalline structure.

questions.q: Which is the most reactive metal?
questions.explanation: Among the given options, as per the reactivity series, potassium (K) is the most reactive metal. It reacts vigorously with air and water, producing a large amount of heat. The ionization energy of potassium is lower than that of sodium because its atomic size is larger. Metals like potassium and sodium react rapidly with cold water. Their reactions are vigorous and exothermic because the released hydrogen ignites immediately. Calcium reacts with water relatively slowly. Magnesium does not react with cold water, but with hot water it produces magnesium hydroxide and hydrogen gas. Metals like aluminium, iron, and zinc do not react with cold or hot water; rather, they react with steam to produce metal oxides and hydrogen. Metals at the top of the reactivity series (K, Na, Ca, Mg, and Al) are so reactive that they are generally not found in the free state. Reactivity Series: Relative reactivity of metals K Potassium Na Sodium Ca Calcium Mg Magnesium Al Aluminium Zn Zinc Fe Iron Pb Lead [H] Hydrogen Cu Copper Hg Mercury Ag Silver Au Gold

questions.q: The cans in which food is packed are coated with tin and not zinc because

options.A: Tin is more reactive than zinc
options.B: Zinc is more reactive than tin
options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than tin; therefore, food cans are coated with tin, not zinc.

questions.q: Food cans are coated with tin and not with zinc because

options.B: Zinc has a higher melting point than tin
options.C: Zinc is more reactive than tin
options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than tin; therefore, food cans are coated with tin, not zinc.

questions.q: Which among the following is also known as white metal?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Basically, white metal is an alloy of lead and tin, or an alloy of other metals such as cadmium, bismuth, and zinc.

questions.q: Which of the following seeds is used in production of engineered diamonds?
questions.explanation: Graphite is used in the production of engineered diamonds. Engineered diamonds are made under conditions of high pressure, high temperature, and chemical vapor deposition

questions.q: Consider the following statements with respect to noble metals: 1. Noble metals are found in pure form in nature. 2. Uranium and lead are examples of noble metals. Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A noble metal is treated as a metallic chemical element. Noble metals are found in nature in pure as well as mixed forms. Uranium and lead are not examples of noble metals.

questions.q: Which one of the following metals is liquid at ordinary temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury is liquid at normal temperature. It is used in thermometers to measure temperature.

questions.q: Lead (Pb) is used for—
questions.explanation: Lead is a metal of bluish-gray colour. It has metallic lustre. Its atomic number in the periodic table is 82 and it is represented by the symbol Pb. Lead is used in electric cables (overhead or underground), in chemical laboratories, and in making bullets. Lead (Pb) is also used for transmission of light.

questions.q: Radium was obtained from which mineral?
questions.explanation: Radium is obtained from pitchblende. Pitchblende is an ore of uranium, but radium is also found in it in very small amounts. The Curie couple processed pitchblende to obtain radium.

questions.q: After being exposed to air for a while, a layer of green basic carbonate forms on a metal; that metal is:
questions.explanation: After being kept in air for some time, a green layer of basic carbonate (copper carbonate and copper hydroxide) forms on copper. In fact, it is the result of oxidation of copper in air.

questions.q: Iron is obtained from which of the following minerals?
questions.explanation: Iron is obtained from the ore hematite (Fe2O3). Other major ores of iron are magnetite (Fe3O4), limonite (FeO(OH)·nH2O), and siderite (FeCO3).

questions.q: What is untrue for bleaching powder?

options.A: It is more soluble in water
options.B: It is powder of light yellow colour
options.D: It releases chlorine after reaction with dilute acid

questions.explanation: Bleaching powder is a pale yellowish-white powder having the smell of chlorine. When bleaching powder is left open in air, chlorine gas slowly escapes from it. It reacts with carbon dioxide or dilute sulphuric acid or dilute hydrochloric acid to liberate chlorine gas. CaOCl2 + CO2 → CaCO3 + Cl2 CaOCl2 + 2HCl → CaCl2 + H2O + Cl2 CaOCl2 + H2SO4 → CaSO4 + H2O + Cl2

questions.q: The metallurgical process in which a metal is obtained in a fused state is called

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In smelting, metal is obtained at high temperature by reduction of the ore. In this process, the metal is obtained in molten (fused), mixed, or pure state.

questions.q: In the method of electroplating on a vessel with zinc

options.A: The vessel is made to be the negative pole.
options.B: Pure zinc is made to the positive pole.
options.C: The vessel is made negative pole and pure zinc as positive pole.
options.D: The pot is made the positive pole and zinc the negative pole.

questions.explanation: In electroplating a vessel with zinc, zinc becomes a cation by losing two electrons, and the vessel becomes negative by gaining electrons. Thus, zinc becomes the positive electrode and the vessel becomes the negative electrode.

questions.q: What happens to the weight of iron, when it rusts?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: When iron rusts, it gets oxidized into hydrated iron oxide (Fe2O3·nH 2O). Due to the addition of oxygen during oxidation, the weight of iron increases; but after a long time, due to rusting, the process of iron getting consumed starts. Because of this, the weight of iron will decrease. The Bihar Public Service Commission, in its final answer key, considered option (a) as the answer.

questions.q: Made of zinc-
questions.explanation: Zinc is mainly extracted from the sulphide ore zinc blende (ZnS). It is a good conductor of heat and electricity. It is used in electric batteries and in making alloys.

questions.q: Al2O3.2SiO2.2H2O is the chemical formula for

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Kaolin was first discovered in Kaoling (China); therefore, it is also called china clay. It is a naturally occurring soft white substance. Its chemical formula is Al2O3·2SiO2·2H2O. Its chemical name is hydrated aluminium silicate.

questions.q: Zinc Oxide is normally used in the manufacture of

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Zinc oxide is an inorganic compound used in many manufacturing processes. It is used in rubber, plastic, ceramics, glass, cement, paints, ointments, food products, batteries, etc. It is also used secondarily in the manufacture of solvents and explosives.

questions.q: The heaviest metal among the following is-
questions.explanation: Among the given options, uranium is the heaviest metal. Its atomic number is 92 and its atomic mass is 238.029 u.

questions.q: Which of the following methods is suitable to prevent an iron frying pan from rusting?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: To prevent an iron frying pan from rusting, a zinc coating is applied. This process is called galvanisation. Zinc is more reactive than iron; therefore, it protects iron from rusting.

questions.q: What is manganese used for?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: The major manganese ore producing states in India are Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. It is used in the manufacture of matches, leather, photography-related materials and dry batteries.

questions.q: What is the common name of Calcium Hydroxide?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: The common name of calcium hydroxide [Ca(OH)2] is slaked lime. Calcium hydroxide is an inorganic compound. In solid form it appears as a white powder, and in crystalline form it is colourless.

questions.q: Standard electrode potential of three metals A, B and C are respectively 0.5 V, -3 V and -1.2 V. Reducing power of these metals would be
questions.explanation: The more negative the standard electrode potential of a metal, the stronger its reducing power. Therefore: Metal Standard electrode potential A 0.5 V B –3 V C –1.2 V Hence, the reducing power is: B > C > A

questions.q: Mercury-metal mixture is –

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A mercury alloy is a mercury-containing alloy.

questions.q: Brass is an alloy of –
questions.explanation: Brass is an alloy made of copper (Cu) and zinc (Zn). Brass is used for making utensils, wires, machines, cartridges, etc. The properties of alloys are generally different from those of their constituent elements; for example, steel is stronger than its main constituent iron.

questions.q: Brass is formed by mixing one volume part of zinc (density 7100 kg/m) with two volume parts of copper (density 8900 kg/m3). The density of brass is -
questions.explanation: 3 parts of brass = 1 part zinc + 2 parts copper = 7100 + 2 × 8900 = 24900 Density of brass = 24900 3 = 8300 kg/m³

questions.q: Stainless steel is an alloy of—
questions.explanation: In general, chromium and nickel are used to make stainless (rust-resistant) steel. By mixing these components with iron, stainless steel is prepared.
questions.note: ⚠ No officially verified answer for this question. Stainless steel's defining alloying element (along with iron) is chromium; nickel is also commonly added, but chromium is what makes it 'stainless'.

questions.q: Stainless steel is an alloy of :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In general, chromium and nickel are used to make stainless (rust-resistant) steel. By mixing these components with iron, stainless steel is prepared.

questions.q: Which of the following metals does not corrode?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Gold and platinum do not corrode. Hence, option (d) is correct.

chapters.chapter_name: A. Carbon and its Various Forms

questions.q: The gas, which comes out on opening a soda water bottle, is :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The gas released on opening a soda water bottle is carbon dioxide (CO2), which remains dissolved in the soda under high pressure.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about graphite and diamond is true?

options.A: They have the same crystal structure.
options.C: They have the same electrical conductivity.
options.D: They can undergo a similar chemical reaction.
options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Graphite and diamond are both allotropes of carbon, but their crystal structures are different. Diamond is naturally the hardest substance, whereas graphite is less hard. Graphite has higher electrical conductivity than diamond. Since both graphite and diamond are made of carbon atoms linked by covalent bonds, their chemical properties are similar and they can undergo the same chemical reactions.

questions.q: Dry ice is –
questions.explanation: Solid carbon dioxide looks like ice; therefore, it is called dry ice. Dry ice sublimates directly into carbon dioxide gas without changing into the liquid state.

questions.q: Which of the following does not consist of carbon?
questions.explanation: Diamond, graphite, and coal are all allotropes of carbon. Therefore, carbon is present in all three.

questions.q: Which is the hardest in the following?
questions.explanation: Diamond is the hardest natural substance. In diamond, each carbon atom is strongly bonded to other carbon atoms. As a result, it has a rigid three-dimensional structure. Due to its hardness, it is used for cutting glass and for making tools that drill holes in hard stones.

questions.q: What is the gas emitted from vehicles?
questions.explanation: Vehicles mainly emit carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, oxides of nitrogen, sulfur dioxide, and hydrocarbons. Therefore, more than one option is correct as the answer to this question.
questions.note: ⚠ No officially verified answer for this question. Carbon monoxide is the standard textbook answer for this question, though vehicles do emit several other gases (CO2, NOx, etc.) too.

questions.q: To make the steel hard requires increase in –
questions.explanation: By adding suitable alloying elements to steel, the required hardness, ductility, and malleability are obtained. The more carbon is added to iron, the harder the steel becomes. However, as hardness increases, brittleness also increases. Manganese is used to increase tensile strength, while nickel is used to make it corrosion-resistant.

questions.q: Catalyst used in hydrogenation of vegetable oil into vanaspati ghee is

options.E: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: To convert vegetable oil into vanaspati ghee, nickel (Ni) is used as a catalyst. The process of converting vegetable oil into ghee is called hydrogenation. In this process, hydrogen gas is mixed with vegetable oil. As a result, the unsaturated fatty acids present in vegetable oil react with hydrogen, and their double bonds are converted into single bonds. This increases the melting point of the oil, and it becomes semisolid at room temperature.

questions.q: The gas used in the manufacture of Vanaspati Ghee from Vanaspati Oil is –
questions.explanation: To convert vegetable oil into vanaspati ghee, nickel (Ni) is used as a catalyst. The process of converting vegetable oil into ghee is called hydrogenation. In this process, hydrogen gas is mixed with vegetable oil. As a result, the unsaturated fatty acids present in vegetable oil react with hydrogen, and their double bonds are converted into single bonds. This increases the melting point of the oil, and it becomes semisolid at room temperature.

questions.q: Diamond is an allotrope (Form) of -
questions.explanation: Diamond is an allotrope of carbon. In diamond, each carbon atom bonds with four other atoms to form a strong threedimensional tetrahedral structure.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about diamond and graphite is true?

options.C: They have same degree of hardness.
options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Diamond and graphite are both known as allotropes of carbon, but neither their crystal structure nor their hardness is the same. In diamond, carbon atoms form a three-dimensional tetrahedral structure, whereas in graphite they form planar hexagonal rings. Diamond is the hardest substance, while graphite is very soft. Similarly, diamond is a poor conductor of electricity, whereas graphite is an excellent conductor. Hence, option (e) is the correct answer.

questions.q: The purest form of the amorphous carbon is

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The purest form of amorphous carbon is lamp black.

questions.q: In the context of lab-grown diamonds (LGDs), what is used as a diamond seed?
questions.explanation: In the context of laboratory-grown diamonds (LGD), graphite is used as the diamond seed. These diamonds are mainly produced by two methods: the High Pressure–High Temperature (HPHT) method or Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD).

questions.q: Fullerene or buckyball is made up of _____carbon atoms.

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Fullerene is an allotrope of carbon, which contains 60 carbon atoms. It is used in semiconductors, lubricants, etc.

chapters.chapter_name: B. Hydrogen and its Various Forms

questions.q: The speed of an electron in the orbit of the hydrogen atom in the ground state is

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: In the ground state, the speed of an electron in the orbit of a hydrogen atom (Z = 1) is c/137 (where c is the speed of light).

questions.q: Burning of hydrogen produces –
questions.explanation: On combustion of hydrogen, water is formed. 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O

questions.q: An element X has four electrons in its outermost orbit. What will be the formula of its compounds with Hydrogen?
questions.explanation: An element having 4 electrons in the outermost shell will form four covalent bonds to attain stability. Hydrogen has one electron in its outermost shell and needs one more electron to become stable. Therefore, four hydrogen atoms will combine with the element having four valence electrons, forming XH4.

questions.q: Which compound is used in contraceptive pills?
questions.explanation: Common oral contraceptive pills and emergency contraceptive pills are mainly based on a synthetic progestogen; the most commonly used compound is levonorgestrel.

questions.q: Heavy water is that water –

options.A: The temperature of which is kept constant at 4°C
options.B: In which insoluble salts of Calcium and Potassium are present
options.C: In which isotopes takes the place of Hydrogen
options.D: In which isotopes takes the place of Oxygen

questions.explanation: Deuterium is an isotope of hydrogen. If water is formed with deuterium in place of ordinary hydrogen, then it is called heavy water. Its chemical formula is D2O.

questions.q: Water gas is a mixture of

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Water gas is a mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen gas (CO + H2), whereas a mixture of carbon monoxide and nitrogen (CO + N2) is called producer gas. The calorific value of water gas is about 2800 kcal/kg. It is used as a reducing agent in the manufacture of hydrogen and alcohol.

chapters.chapter_name: C. Sulphur, Nitrogen, Halogen, Inert gases

questions.q: Bromine is-

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Bromine is a dark reddish-brown, volatile liquid with a sharp smell. Bromine (Br) has atomic number 35 and remains in the liquid state at room temperature. It is non-flammable and slightly soluble in water. Bromine is a member of group 17, which is also known as the halogen group.

questions.q: Human skin burns during swimming in lake/ pond -
questions.explanation: Human skin burns during swimming in lake/pond because chlorine (Cl2) is used for purification of lake water. Due to excess chlorine, the skin gets burnt.

questions.q: Hydrofluoric acid is not kept in a glass bottle because it reacts with
questions.explanation: Hydrofluoric acid is not kept in a glass. Hydrofluoric acid (HF) is a highly reactive compound. It reacts with the silicon dioxide of glass, due to which the bottle gets corroded.

questions.q: What is the shape of a sulfur hexafluoride molecule?
questions.explanation: The shape of sulfur hexafluoride is octahedral.

questions.q: Which is used as laughing gas –
questions.explanation: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is “laughing gas”. It causes laughter when inhaled. Doctors also use it as an anesthetic.

questions.q: pH value of 0.1 N HCl solution is approximately:
questions.explanation: The pH of an aqueous solution is calculated by the following formula: pH = – log10 [H+] In 0.1 N HCl solution— [H+] = 0.1 mol L–¹ Calculation of pH: pH = – log10 (0.1) = – log10 (10–¹) = – (–1) = 1 Thus, the pH of 0.1 N HCl is 1.0, which matches option (b).

questions.q: Which of the following has pH value 7?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A neutral solution has pH 7. Pure water is considered neutral. At 25°C, pure water has pH 7. Rainwater is a pure form of water. A solution with pH more than 7 is alkaline, and a solution with pH less than 7 is acidic.
questions.note: ⚠ No officially verified answer for this question. Both 'Pure Water' (a) and 'Neutral solution' (b) have pH 7 and are simultaneously correct, so option (e) 'more than one of the above' is the best fit.

questions.q: Which of the following solutions has a pH value more than 7?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A neutral solution has pH 7. Pure water is considered neutral. At 25°C, pure water has pH 7. Rainwater is a pure form of water. A solution with pH more than 7 is alkaline, and a solution with pH less than 7 is acidic.

questions.q: The pH value of water is

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A neutral solution has pH 7. Pure water is considered neutral. At 25°C, pure water has pH 7. Rainwater is a pure form of water. A solution with pH more than 7 is alkaline, and a solution with pH less than 7 is acidic.

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic property of an acid?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: The pH value of an acid is less than 7, and it turns blue litmus red, whereas the pH value of a base is greater than 7, and it turns red litmus blue.

questions.q: Lightweight bullet proof helmets and jackets use which of the following fibres for their production?
questions.explanation: Kevlar fibre is used for the construction of lightweight bulletproof helmets and jackets. Kevlar is a strong, heatresistant (thermal-resistant), and synthetic fiber.

questions.q: What is the usual property of oxides of Group 3 and 4?
questions.explanation: The general property of the oxides of the third and fourth groups is that they show both basic and acidic behavior.

questions.q: What substance forms an acid when heated with another substance?'
questions.explanation: Among the given options, heating ammonium chloride with another substance leads to the formation of an acid.

questions.q: Some metal oxides react with acid as well as base to produce salt and water. They are known as amphoteric oxides. The examples of amphoteric oxides are

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: The correct answer is option (b) Al2O3 and ZnO. Some metal oxides react with both acids and bases to form salt and water; these are known as amphoteric oxides. Some oxides can act as both acidic and basic (amphoteric). CuO is basic in nature; hence, it is not amphoteric.

questions.q: Acids react with metal carbonates to liberate ______ gas.

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Acids react with metal carbonates to release carbon dioxide gas; along with this, metal salts and water are also formed. Sodium carbonate reacts with hydrochloric acid to form sodium chloride, carbon dioxide, and water.

questions.q: You have been provided with three test tubes. One of them contains distilled water and the other two contain an acidic solution and a basic solution, respectively. Which of them will turn red litmus to blue?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: In an acidic medium, red litmus does not change color. In a basic medium, red litmus turns blue, and in a neutral medium, neither red nor blue litmus changes colour.

questions.q: Why does dry HCl gas not change the color of dry litmus paper?

options.A: HCl gas acts as a dehydrating agent.
options.B: Blue litmus becomes dry in the presence of dry HCl gas.
options.C: No H3O+ ions are present. Litmus changes color only in the presence of H3O+ ions.
options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Litmus paper changes color only in the presence of ions such as hydrogen (H+) or hydronium (H3O+). HCl can produce these ions only in aqueous solution. Therefore, dry HCl gas does not change the colour of dry litmus paper.

questions.explanation: A salt formed by the reaction between a strong acid and a strong base is called a neutral salt, e.g., NaCl, KNO3.

questions.q: Which is the fundamental element of all organic compounds?
questions.explanation: All living matter in the world is made of organic compounds. Carbon is necessarily present in organic compounds, but not all compounds containing carbon are organic, e.g., CO2, CO, etc.

questions.q: What is/are the full form(s) of HMX? 1. High Melting Explosive 2. High-Density Monoatomic Xenon 3. Hedge Monetizing Xenocurrency 4. Her Majesty’s Explosive Select the correct answer using the codes given below
questions.explanation: H.M.X. (Octogen) is the abbreviation of High Melting Explosive. It is also known as Octogen and Cyclotetramethylene-tetranitramine. It is a colorless solid, slightly soluble in water. It is used in various types of explosives and in rocket fuels.

questions.q: How is Hydrogen stored physically?
questions.explanation: Physically, hydrogen is stored by compressing hydrogen gas at high pressure. However, some transition metals such as Pd and Pt can absorb a large volume of H2 in their hydrides; when these hydrides are heated, they release H2 gas again. Hence, metal hydrides can also be used for hydrogen storage.

questions.q: Oxygen is absent in-

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Among the given options, oxygen is absent in kerosene. Chemically, kerosene (lamp oil) is a mixture of hydrocarbons. Note that hydrocarbons are compounds made only of carbon and hydrogen.

questions.q: Which of the following gases is used in cigarette lighters?
questions.explanation: Butane is a flammable hydrocarbon whose molecular formula is C4H10. It is used in cigarette lighters.

questions.q: Number of sigma and pi bonds in benzene are:

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Benzene is a hydrocarbon with the formula C6H6. It contains six carbon atoms and six hydrogen atoms. Each carbon atom is bonded to one hydrogen atom by a single bond and to two neighboring carbon atoms. The fourth valency of carbon is considered to be involved in a double-bond arrangement. Hence, benzene has twelve sigma bonds and three pi bonds.

questions.q: Alcohol can be converted to carboxylic acid -

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Alcohol (R–CH2–OH) can be converted into a carboxylic acid (R – C – OH ) O only by oxidation. Oxidation is a chemical reaction.

questions.q: Fermentation of sugar leads to –
questions.explanation: By the fermentation of sugar/sucrose (C12H22O11), ethyl alcohol (C2H5OH) is formed.

questions.q: Natural rubber is a polymer of

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Polymerization is a reaction in which two or more molecules of the same kind join together to form a large molecule of higher molecular mass. The molecules participating in polymerization are called monomers, and the product is called a polymer. Natural rubber is the polymer of isoprene. Isoprene is an organic compound with the formula. CH2 = C(CH3) – CH = CH2.

questions.q: Teflon is a polymer of which of the following monomers?

options.E: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) is commonly known as Teflon. PTFE is a solid fluorocarbon. Its density is 2.2 g/cm³ and its melting point is about 327°C. It is mainly used as a non-stick coating on utensils.

questions.q: Bakelite is formed by the condensation of :

options.E: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Bakelite is the first completely synthetic plastic made by humans. Its chemical name is polyoxybenzylmethylene glycol anhydride. It is a thermosetting phenol–formaldehyde resin, formed by condensation polymerization of phenol and formaldehyde.

questions.q: What is the ‘fiber’ used to make bulletproof jackets?
questions.explanation: Kevlar is used to make bulletproof jackets. Kevlar is a polyamide, which is a type of polymer. It is a heat-resistant and high-strength synthetic polymer. Para-phenylenediamine and terephthaloyl chloride are the two monomers of Kevlar.

questions.q: Which one of the following is an example of melamine used for making floor tiles ?
questions.explanation: Melamine is a thermosetting plastic. A thermosetting plastic is a man-made material that, once molded, cannot be reheated and reshaped. Thermosetting plastics can withstand high temperatures without losing their shape.

questions.q: Which of the following gases is used to artificially ripen fruits?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Ethylene gas is used to artificially ripen fruits. Ethylene is a gaseous plant hormone that plays an important role in triggering the fruit-ripening process.

questions.q: Lemon is citrus due to –
questions.explanation: Lemon contains citric acid, which makes it taste sour.

questions.explanation: HOOCCOOH (Oxalic acid) is a dicarboxylic acid whose chemical formula is C2H2O4. It is also known as ethanedioic acid or oxalic acid. questions.q: What was the fissionable material used in the bombs dropped at Nagasaki (Japan) in the year 1945?
questions.explanation: On 9 August, 1945, a bomb named “Fat Man” was dropped on Nagasaki (Japan). Plutonium was used in it as the explosive material. On the other hand, on 6 August, 1945, the bomb dropped on Hiroshima, named “Little Boy”, used uranium as the explosive material.

questions.explanation: Nitroglycerin is an ester, which is used as an explosive.

questions.q: The device which converts chemical energy of fuels directly into electrical energy is

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A fuel cell is an electrochemical device that converts the chemical energy obtained from fuel directly into electrical energy. A fuel cell produces electric current by combining hydrogen and oxygen, and water is formed as a byproduct in this process. Like an ordinary battery, a fuel cell also converts chemical energy into electrical energy; however, it does not store energy.

questions.q: Which of the following is the major constituent of liquefied petroleum gas?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The main constituents of LPG are butane (about 65%) and propane (about 35%). Other hydrocarbons, such as ethane, may also be present in small amounts.

questions.q: LPG used as domestic fuel mainly contains :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: LPG, i.e., liquefied petroleum gas, used as a domestic fuel, is a flammable mixture of hydrocarbons gases. It mainly contains a mixture of propane (C3H8) and butane (C4H10). questions.q: The incomplete burning of petrol and diesel produces :

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Due to lack of oxygen, complete combustion of petrol or diesel cannot occur in the engine; therefore, mainly carbon monoxide is produced and emitted.

questions.q: Which compound is used for increase of octane rating?
questions.explanation: Octane rating is a measure of petrol’s ability (quality) to burn in a controlled manner during compression without causing engine knocking. Tetraethyl lead was used to increase the octane rating of petrol; it reduced engine knock, and the engine could run more smoothly at higher compression. questions.explanation: Petrol is generally used in motor cars. Gasoline or petrol is a liquid mixture obtained from petroleum; petrol is also used as a powerful solvent.

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The composition and physical properties of potassium iodide (KI) are similar to those of table salt. At the commercial level, it is generally used for making iodized salt. In addition, potassium iodate, sodium iodate, and sodium iodide are also used for making iodised salt.

questions.q: What is a triglyceride?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Triglyceride is a type of fat found in the body. Our body converts unused energy obtained from food into triglycerides. Triglycerides are stored in fat cells.

questions.q: The artificial sweetener containing chlorine that has the appearance and taste as that of sugar and remains stable at cooking temperature, is

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Sucralose is an artificial sweetener and a substitute for sugar. Most ingested sucralose is not broken down by the body; therefore, it is non-caloric. questions.q: Which one of the following substances is used in the preservation of foodstuff?
questions.explanation: Sodium benzoate is used for food preservation. Its chemical formula is C6H5COONa.

questions.q: What is the basis of most useful classification of medications in medical chemistry?
questions.explanation: In medicinal chemistry, drugs are classified on the basis of chemical structure, pharmacological effect, solubility, and molecular target. Among these, classification based on the molecular target is considered the most useful.

questions.q: 100% Pure ethanol is called ________ .'
questions.explanation: 100% pure ethanol (C2H5OH) is called absolute alcohol. It is prepared from rectified spirit. It is used in medicine, organic chemistry, etc. Due to its flammability and high calorific value, it can also be used as an alternative fuel for gasoline in combustion engines.

questions.q: The term ‘green chemistry’ refers to–

options.A: a process of synthesizing chemical compounds by minimizing the use of hazardous chemicals
options.B: innovative scientific solutions to real-world environmental problems
options.C: the process that reduces the negative impact of chemical processes on human health and environment
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Green chemistry is the design of chemical products and processes that reduce or eliminate the use or generation of hazardous substances. With the help of green chemistry, solutions to environmental problems can be achieved. It reduces negative impacts on human health and the environment. Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.q: Detergents used for cleaning clothes are :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Detergents are surfactants (wetting-agent) compounds that show cleaning properties in dilute solution. In fact, such substances are alkyl benzene sulfonates. Detergents are soluble even in hard water.

questions.q: Soap removes grease by-

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Emulsification is the process of mixing two or more immiscible liquids to form a semi-stable mixture. Soap molecules are generally long-chain compounds with polar groups; for example, soap (fatty salts of sodium and potassium). A soap molecule has two parts- (i) a long hydrocarbon chain (C17H35) which is soluble in fat, and (ii) a water-soluble polar part (–COO– Na+ group). During emulsification, the non-polar alkyl part (C17H35) dissolves oil or grease, while the polar part (–COO– Na+) dissolves in water. When rubbed properly, grease becomes suspended in water as tiny droplets and is easily washed away with running water.

questions.q: What is detergent?
questions.explanation: Substances used for cleaning are called soaps and detergents. In fact, the soap that we have been using for years also falls under the detergent category.

questions.q: Which one of the following is used in the manufacture of soaps?
questions.explanation: When an oil or fat is mixed with sodium hydroxide solution, the oil/fat gets converted into the corresponding sodium salts of fatty acids and glycerol. This reaction is called saponification.

questions.q: Permanent hardness of water is due to –

options.A: Chlorides and sulphates of Calcium and Magnesium

questions.explanation: Hard water is water that does not produce lather easily when detergent (soap) is used. The main cause of this is the presence of chlorides and sulphates of calcium and magnesium.

questions.q: The elements present in urea are :

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Urea is an organic compound with the chemical formula NH2CONH2. It contains about 46.67% nitrogen, present in the form of an amide. In organic chemistry, it is also called carbamide.

questions.q: Which component of fertilizer is used to encourage rapid development?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus helps in transferring energy from sunlight to plants, stimulates early root and plant growth, and speeds up maturity. Hence, option (d) is correct. Apart from phosphorus, nitrogen, potassium, etc., also help in plant growth.

questions.q: Which compound is known as a night-glowing pigment from below?
questions.explanation: Night-glowing pigments are substances that first absorb light energy and then keep emitting light slowly for a long time in darkness. Among the given options, europium-doped strontium aluminate is well-known and widely used as a night-glowing pigment.

questions.q: Which material is used for smart film?
questions.explanation: Smart film or switchable smart film is generally a PDLC (Polymer Dispersed Liquid Crystal) film. For the transparent conductive layer of smart film, indium tin oxide (ITO)-coated PET or glass is commonly used. Calcium carbonate (CaCO3) is mainly used in cement, lime making, and as a filler; zinc chloride (ZnCl2) is used in chemical reactions, dry cells, flux, etc.; and silica (SiO2) is used as a structural material for ordinary glass, etc.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a radioactive element?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Cadmium is classified as a transition metal, and cadmium is a chemical element; however, it is not a radioactive element. Cadmium (Cd) is a silver-colored metal with a bluish tinge. Cadmium is a toxic metal. Its most common use is in the manufacture of nickel–cadmium batteries.

questions.q: Which of the following is the best fire extinguisher?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Among the given options, carbon dioxide (CO2) is a good fire extinguisher. Carbon dioxide is commonly used in fire extinguishers.

questions.q: The breath test conducted by police to check a drunken driver has which one of the following on the filter paper?

options.C: Silica gel coated with silver nitrate
options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: To test the breath of a person suspected of drunk driving, the police use an instrument called a breathalyzer (breathalyser). In this device, the filter paper/chemical cartridge contains potassium dichromate (K2Cr2O7) and sulfuric acid (H2SO4). The orange-red potassium dichromate reagent reacts with alcohol and turns green. The intensity of the green color is used to estimate the amount of alcohol in the exhaled breath.

questions.q: The alphabet X in X-ray stands for _______ ray.

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In X-rays, the letter X means an unknown ray. X-rays are a type of electromagnetic radiation.
